title: Why Doesn't Your Stomach Digest Itself?

shots.line: Why doesn't your stomach digest itself?
shots.scene: Wide night kitchen, one cold lamp over the counter, hero at the island turning the question over. Slow push-in.

shots.line: It's bathed in acid around pH one point five,
shots.scene: Blueprint body outline, stomach drawn in glowing acid-green, callout GASTRIC ACID, pH meter filling.
Acid layer above the gut wall eats an iron nail; it shrinks, sparks, glow blooms. Badge pH 1.5.
Giant face close-up, blurred kitchen behind, brows up, lip-synced to the real word timings.
Pull-out reveal of the gut wall: mucus line, nine tissue cells in a row, callout MUCOSAL LINING.

shots.line: Every few days, your stomach grows a brand new surface, cell by cell,
shots.scene: New cells pop in one after another beneath the row, each with a white ring; data card counts 0 to 9.
Old cells lift off the wall and drift up into the acid, fading; droplets hang in the layer.

shots.line: But when that rebuild slows, an ulcer, or too many painkillers,
shots.scene: One cell is missing from the row, red ring around the gap, pills fall in from above. Slight camera roll.

shots.line: the acid reaches the tissue underneath.
shots.scene: Acid pours through the breach as a bright column, red glow spreads into the tissue, camera shake on impact.

shots.line: And then it does what you'd expect. It digests you.
shots.scene: Giant face, warm-red rim, blurred breached wall behind; then cut to the hero arms-crossed with the end question.
